key_provisions_or_claims: Devices may be placed on the market only if they do not compromise patient, user or third-party safety and meet Annex I essential requirements.
Devices are classified into Classes I, IIa, IIb and III with conformity assessment routes scaled to risk, involving notified bodies.
CE marking is required and gives free movement across Member States; harmonised standards confer presumption of conformity.
Manufacturers and Member States must record and report serious incidents (vigilance system).
Clinical investigations require notification, ethics committee opinion and compliance with the Helsinki Declaration.
annotation.summary_en: Council Directive 93/42/EEC harmonises EU rules on medical devices: essential safety and performance requirements, four risk classes, notified-body conformity assessment, CE marking, vigilance reporting and clinical investigation rules. Not AI-specific, but it is the legacy framework for actuated medical devices, including software, later replaced by the Medical Devices Regulation.
